name: Motion
summary: Durations and easing curves, the state transitions of controls, and how motion gives way when people ask for less of it.
description: Motion holds two durations and one easing curve, the design system's additions (packages/tokens/src/additions/): the Figma library has none. Components read them directly for one use: the transition of a control between its states. Every transition is a color change, never a movement, and every component switches it off when people ask for reduced motion.

rules.name: Primitives
rules.text: Two durations (fast, normal) and one easing curve (standard).

rules.name: Control transitions
rules.text: Controls transition their colors (fill, border, text) between states over the fast duration, with the standard easing.

rules.name: Color, not movement
rules.text: Transitions change colors only: nothing slides, scales or moves when a control changes state.

rules.name: Never the only cue
rules.text: Motion is feedback, never information: every state is understandable without its transition.

rules.name: Reduced motion
rules.text: When people ask their system for reduced motion, components drop their transitions and change state instantly.

rules.name: Web rendering
rules.text: CSS transition on the component, reading its transition tokens, and a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce rule setting transition to none. The validator requires that rule whenever a component's CSS transitions or animates.

specimens.name: Durations
specimens.description: Each duration moves a dot across the track at constant speed.

specimens.name: Easing curves
specimens.description: Each curve, and a dot following it over one second, slowed down so the curve shows.

guidelines.text: Motion triggered by an interaction can be turned off: every transition of the system stops when people ask for reduced motion (WCAG 2.3.3, AAA, adopted as extra quality).
Motion is optional and never the only way to communicate: a state reads the same without its transition.
Components read prefers-reduced-motion and set their transitions to none under reduce.
When the Reduce Motion setting is on, automatic and repetitive animations are reduced.

references.title: WCAG technique C39: Using the CSS prefers-reduced-motion query to prevent motion

changelog.note: Breaking: the semantic motion.control.* tokens, invented by the repository, are removed; components alias duration.fast and easing.standard directly (the design system's additions, unchanged values). No visual change.
Initial draft: the motion primitives and the control transition as they are, specified once (no token changes).
